newsitem.title: USA: US, Japan firms debate 100-125 yen range - Lucent CEO.
newsitem.headline: US, Japan firms debate 100-125 yen range - Lucent CEO.

text.p: Lucent Technologies Inc Chairman Henry Schacht said Wednesday he believed both U.S. and Japanese companies would be comfortable with a yen-dollar exchange rate somewhere in the middle of the 100 to 125 yen range.
Speaking to reporters at a U.S.-Japan business conference in San Francisco, Schacht said he had heard executives talk of optimum dollar rates ranging from 100 to 125 yen with a midpoint around 115.

"I think most U.S. companies would be on one side of that discussion and most Japanese companies would be on the other side," said Schacht. "I would suspect we'd both come out somewhere in the middle of that range and be comfortable."

"Obviously the key is having the markets find -- because I believe that's exactly how it will be set -- a range that will accommodate both Japan's requirements for internal growth and avoid lurching back into an exchange rate that would cause an exacerbation of the trade imbalances, and therefore get us back into the discussion that all of us thought we had behind us for a while," he said.
Exchange rates have been a key topic of discussion at the two-day meeting of U.S. and Japanese business people here, organized by the U.S.-Japan and Japan-U.S. business councils.

Schacht said he believed the market would determine what was a good level for the dollar-yen exchange rate. "Despite all the nudging and talking I think the market will finally have its way and I think we'll have to wait and see," he said.

"The final determination will be how it affects the trade balance or imbalance. If we begin to drift into very large imbalances again, I think the debate will start all over again," he said. "Most of us are happy to get that debate behind us and get on with more useful kinds of things to talk about."
